regulatory_bodies.name: Instituto de Salud Pública de Chile
regulatory_bodies.description: Chile's public health institute regulates pharmaceuticals, medical devices, and health products. Issues ISP registrations under the Sanitary Code (DFL No. 725/1967). Strong regional leadership.

regulatory_bodies.name: Agencia Chilena para la Inocuidad y Calidad Alimentaria
regulatory_bodies.description: Chile's food safety and quality agency coordinates food safety policy. SEREMI de Salud and SAG enforce food regulations at local level.

regulatory_bodies.name: Dirección General de Medicamentos, Insumos y Drogas
regulatory_bodies.description: Peru's general directorate for medicines, supplies and drugs under the Ministry of Health. Issues Registro Sanitario for pharmaceuticals, medical devices, and health products.

regulatory_bodies.name: Dirección General de Salud Ambiental e Inocuidad Alimentaria
regulatory_bodies.description: Peru's food safety and environmental health directorate. Issues Registro Sanitario for food products including health supplements.

regulatory_bodies.name: Agencia Nacional de Regulación, Control y Vigilancia Sanitaria
regulatory_bodies.description: Ecuador's comprehensive national health regulation agency. Regulates food, drugs, cosmetics, and medical devices under LOSSANE.

regulatory_bodies.name: Agencia Estatal de Medicamentos y Tecnologías en Salud
regulatory_bodies.description: Bolivia's state agency for medicines and health technologies. Issues pharmaceutical registrations under Ley del Medicamento No. 1737/1996.

regulatory_bodies.name: Instituto Boliviano de Normalización y Calidad
regulatory_bodies.description: Bolivia's national standards and quality institute sets food standards. Food safety enforcement by SENASAG (food/agricultural products).

regulatory_bodies.name: Dirección Nacional de Vigilancia Sanitaria
regulatory_bodies.description: Paraguay's national health surveillance directorate under MSPBS. Issues Registros Sanitarios for all health products under MERCOSUR harmonised framework.

regulatory_bodies.name: Ministerio de Salud Pública Uruguay — Departamento de Medicamentos
regulatory_bodies.description: Uruguay's Ministry of Public Health regulates pharmaceuticals and health products. MERCOSUR harmonisation applies extensively. Strong institutional capacity.

regulatory_bodies.name: Laboratorio Tecnológico del Uruguay
regulatory_bodies.description: Uruguay's state technology laboratory supports food safety standards. MGAP (Ministry of Livestock, Agriculture) and MSP jointly regulate food.

regulatory_bodies.name: Ministerio del Poder Popular para la Salud Venezuela
regulatory_bodies.description: Venezuela's Ministry of Health and Social Protection regulates pharmaceuticals and food. Regulatory capacity significantly impacted by economic conditions since 2015.

regulatory_bodies.name: Ministerio de Salud Pública y Asistencia Social Guatemala
regulatory_bodies.description: Guatemala's Ministry of Public Health. DQFB (Drug, Food and Beverage Regulation Directorate) issues Registros Sanitarios for health products.

regulatory_bodies.name: Secretaría de Salud Honduras
regulatory_bodies.description: Honduras Ministry of Health regulates pharmaceuticals and food. ARSA (National Agency for Food and Drug Regulation) was created 2019 to strengthen regulatory capacity.

regulatory_bodies.name: Ministerio de Salud Costa Rica — DNIV
regulatory_bodies.description: Costa Rica's Ministry of Health Directorate of National Health Surveillance (DNIV). Issues health registrations. Costa Rica has one of the strongest regulatory frameworks in Central America.

regulatory_bodies.name: Ministerio de Salud Panamá — DNFD
regulatory_bodies.description: Panama's Ministry of Health, National Directorate of Pharmacy and Drugs (DNFD). Issues health product registrations. Panama Free Trade Zone (Colón) significant for regional distribution.

regulatory_bodies.name: Centro para el Control Estatal de Medicamentos Cuba
regulatory_bodies.description: Cuba's state centre for drug control. Cuba has a unique pharmaceutical system with significant domestic biotechnology capacity. Very restrictive import market.

regulatory_bodies.name: Ministerio de Salud Pública Dominican Republic
regulatory_bodies.description: Dominican Republic's Ministry of Public Health. DIGEMAPS issues drug registrations. SESPAS has been strengthening its regulatory framework with WHO/PAHO support.

regulatory_bodies.name: Ministerio de Salud Nicaragua — CRNM
regulatory_bodies.description: Nicaragua's Ministry of Health Centre for Regulatory and Normative Resources (CRNM) issues pharmaceutical registrations.

licensing_pathways.license_type: Registro Sanitario — Suplemento Alimenticio (ISP/Seremi de Salud)
licensing_pathways.competent_authority: ISP (Instituto de Salud Pública de Chile)
pathway_steps: 1. Classify as Alimento para Fines Especiales — Suplemento Alimenticio under Reglamento Sanitario de los Alimentos (RSA)
2. Verify formulation complies with RSA (Decreto 977/1996) Chapter 17 (Special Purpose Foods)
3. Appoint Chilean importer or local legal representative
4. Prepare dossier: formulation, label, CoA, safety data
5. Submit Registro Sanitario application to ISP
6. ISP technical review: 60–120 working days
7. Receive RS number
8. Label in Spanish with RS number and all mandatory declarations

gmp_requirements.standard: GMP equivalent to Codex Alimentarius General Principles of Food Hygiene

renewal_requirements: Apply before expiry; fee payment required
licensing_pathways.reference_regulation: Decreto 977/1996 Reglamento Sanitario de los Alimentos (RSA); Código Sanitario DFL No. 725/1967
licensing_pathways.notes: Chile has a front-of-pack black octagonal warning seal system (HIGH IN: calories, sugars, saturated fat, sodium, trans fat) mandatory since 2016 — the first country to implement such a system, later adopted by Mexico, Colombia, Peru, and others.

licensing_pathways.license_type: Registro Sanitario — Alimentos de Uso Médico Especial y Suplementos Nutricionales
licensing_pathways.competent_authority: DIGESA (Dirección General de Salud Ambiental) and DIGEMID for health products
pathway_steps: 1. Classify: Suplemento Nutricional (nutritional supplement) vs Alimento para Regímenes Especiales
2. Appoint Peruvian importer and Technical Director (Químico-Farmacéutico required)
3. All ingredients must comply with DIGESA/DIGEMID permitted list
4. Prepare dossier per DIGESA requirements: technical file, formulation, safety data
5. Submit RS application — DIGESA for food supplements; DIGEMID if pharmaceutical claims
6. Technical review and laboratory testing may be required
7. Receive Registro Sanitario (RS) number
8. Spanish-language label with RS number, Peruvian importer, and octagonal warning seals (mandatory since 2021)
documents_required: Label draft (with octagonal seals if required)

gmp_requirements.standard: GMP per Codex Alimentarius; DIGESA/DIGEMID may require WHO-GMP for imports

licensing_pathways.reference_regulation: Ley de Inocuidad de los Alimentos DL 1062; DS 007-98-SA (Reglamento de Vigilancia y Control Sanitario de Alimentos); DS 038-2014-SA (Suplementos Nutricionales); Ley 30021 (Alimentación Saludable — octagonal seals)
licensing_pathways.notes: Peru's Ley 30021 (Healthy Eating Law) mandated front-of-pack octagonal warning labels since June 2021, similar to Chile. Advertising of unhealthy foods to children is heavily restricted. Compliance requires both RS and warning seal implementation.

licensing_pathways.license_type: Notificación Sanitaria Obligatoria (NSO) or Registro Sanitario
licensing_pathways.competent_authority: ARCSA (Agencia Nacional de Regulación, Control y Vigilancia Sanitaria)
pathway_steps: 1. Classify product under ARCSA categories: Registro Sanitario (RS) or Notificación Sanitaria Obligatoria (NSO) for lower-risk products
2. NSO: for food products meeting specific criteria — faster 30-day process
3. RS: for supplements, cosmetics with claims — standard process
4. Appoint Ecuadorian distributor/importer
5. Submit via ARCSA online system with required dossier
6. ARCSA review and approval
7. Receive RS or NSO number
8. Spanish-language label with ARCSA authorization number
licensing_pathways.fast_track_details: NSO (Notificación Sanitaria Obligatoria) is a faster track for food products meeting standard ingredient criteria.

gmp_requirements.standard: Buenas Prácticas de Manufactura per ARCSA technical norms

licensing_pathways.reference_regulation: Ley Orgánica de Salud 67/2006; LOSSANE (Ley Orgánica del Régimen de la Soberanía Alimentaria); ARCSA Technical Norms
licensing_pathways.notes: Ecuador adopted octagonal front-of-pack warning labels in 2020 (Reglamento Técnico Ecuatoriano RTE INEN 022). All food products must carry octagonal seals for excess sugar, fat, salt, trans fat, or calories. One of the first countries after Chile to implement this system.

licensing_pathways.competent_authority: MSP (Ministerio de Salud Pública) — Departamento de Vigilancia Sanitaria
pathway_steps: 1. Classify as Suplemento Dietario under Decreto 008/2020 (MSP)
2. Verify MERCOSUR GMC Resolution 58/10 and 82/96 for dietary supplements
3. Appoint Uruguayan Technical Director (farmacéutico)
4. Submit habilitación application to MSP
5. MSP technical review
6. Receive habilitación number
7. Spanish-language label with Uruguay habilitación number

gmp_requirements.standard: BPM per Codex and MERCOSUR norms

licensing_pathways.reference_regulation: Decreto 008/2020 (Suplementos Dietarios); MERCOSUR GMC Resolution 58/10; Código Bromatológico
licensing_pathways.notes: Uruguay has adopted octagonal front-of-pack warning seals (Decreto 117/018) — mandatory for excess sugar, sodium, saturated fat, trans fat, and calories. MERCOSUR harmonisation means Argentina and Brazil alignment is important.

licensing_pathways.competent_authority: MINSA — Dirección de Servicios de Salud (Costa Rica)
pathway_steps: 1. Classify product under Costa Rica's Ley General de Salud No. 5395
2. Appoint Costa Rican importer registered with MINSA
3. Prepare dossier under RTCA (Central American Technical Regulation on food supplements)
4. Submit Registro Sanitario application to MINSA
5. MINSA technical review: 30–60 working days (by law)
6. Receive RS number
7. Label in Spanish with RS number
prerequisites: Costa Rican importer with MINSA registration

gmp_requirements.standard: GMP per RTCA Central American technical regulations

licensing_pathways.reference_regulation: Ley General de Salud No. 5395; RTCA 67.04.54:10 (Suplementos Alimenticios)
licensing_pathways.notes: Costa Rica uses RTCA (Reglamento Técnico Centroamericano) — a harmonised Central American technical regulation system covering food, drugs, and supplements. RTCA allows some mutual recognition within the CACM (Central American Common Market).

allowable_limits.notes: Chile follows Codex GSFA for most additive limits. RSA Chapter XII governs preservatives.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: Codex GSFA (adopted by reference in Peru RS regulations)
allowable_limits.notes: Peru food additive limits generally follow Codex GSFA by regulatory reference. DIGESA publishes specific list of permitted additives.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: RSA Chile — Contaminantes en Alimentos; SEREMIA enforcement
allowable_limits.notes: Chile RSA Chapter XIV sets contaminant limits. Front-of-pack labelling system (octagonal seals) focuses on nutrient content rather than contaminants.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: NTS 071-MINSA/DIGESA — Vigilancia y Control de Alimentos
allowable_limits.notes: Peru's food safety surveillance includes heavy metal testing. DIGESA enforces at point of manufacture and import.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: RSA Chile — Contaminantes: Micotoxinas en Alimentos
allowable_limits.notes: Chile follows Codex mycotoxin limits. Major concern for imported peanuts and corn. SAG enforces at border for agricultural products.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: NTS DIGESA — Mycotoxin Limits in Foods
allowable_limits.notes: Peru has significant mycotoxin burden in domestic maize. DIGESA enforces mycotoxin limits at food processing facilities.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: RSA Chile — Normas Microbiológicas para Alimentos (ICMSF criteria)
allowable_limits.notes: Chile applies ICMSF-based microbiological criteria. ISP coordinates national foodborne illness surveillance.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: NTS No. 071-MINSA/DIGESA — Microbiological Criteria for Foods
allowable_limits.notes: Peru's DIGESA sets microbiological criteria per NTS 071 based on ICMSF. Zero tolerance for Salmonella in RTE foods.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: RSA Chile — Valores de Referencia de Nutrientes (VRN)
allowable_limits.notes: Chile VRN: Vitamin C 60 mg/day. Used for % VRN calculation on octagonal-seal compliant nutrition labels.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: RSA Chile — Tabla de Valores de Referencia de Nutrientes
allowable_limits.notes: Chile: sodium DRV 2000 mg/day. Front-of-pack seal threshold: >800 mg per 100g ALTO EN SODIO. Chile octagonal seal is now mandatory on many products.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: Peru DS 038-2014-SA; Ley 30021 Octagonal Seal Thresholds
allowable_limits.notes: Peru: sodium DRV 2000 mg/day. Octagonal warning seal HIGH IN SODIUM triggered at >400 mg/100g (solid) or >100 mg/100mL (liquid) — stricter threshold than Chile.
Chile permits tartrazine at Codex-aligned levels. Chilean RSA specifies colour limits by food category.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: Chile SAG — MRLs for Pesticides in Foods (Resolución Exenta)
allowable_limits.notes: Chile sets MRLs via SAG (Servicio Agrícola y Ganadero). Chile re-evaluated glyphosate ADI at 0.3 mg/kg bw/day (lower than EU). Monitoring programme for soybean imports.

allowable_limits.regulatory_basis: RSA Chile — Metales Pesados en Productos Pesqueros; SERNAPESCA
allowable_limits.notes: Chile is a major fishing nation. SERNAPESCA (fisheries authority) and RSA jointly regulate mercury in fish. Strict monitoring of corvina, atún, and pez espada (swordfish).

labeling_requirements.regulatory_basis: Ley 20.606 (Alimentación Saludable 2012); DS No. 13/2015 (Reglamento Ley 20.606); RSA Decreto 977/1996
labeling_requirements.competent_authority: MINSAL (Ministerio de Salud); SEREMI de Salud for enforcement; ISP for RS
mandatory_fields: Lista de ingredientes (ingredients descending by weight)
País de origen (country of origin for imports)
Fecha de elaboración y vencimiento (production and expiry date)
Sellos de advertencia (ALTO EN: octagonal black warning seals — MANDATORY if thresholds exceeded)
Número de Registro Sanitario (RS number from ISP)

nutrition_declaration.format: Per 100g/100mL. % VRN (Valor de Referencia de Nutrientes). Standard table format. Black octagonal ALTO EN seals mandatory on front of pack if energy >350 kcal/100g, sugars >22.5g/100g, saturated fat >6g/100g, sodium >800mg/100g, trans fat present.
nutrition_declaration.nrv_reference: Chile RSA — Tabla de Valores de Referencia de Nutrientes (VRN)
nutrition_declaration.warning_seals: ALTO EN: CALORÍAS (>350 kcal/100g), AZÚCARES (>22.5g/100g), GRASAS SATURADAS (>6g/100g), SODIO (>800mg/100g), GRASAS TRANS (any). Black octagonal seals with white text on FRONT of package.

top_allergens: Cereales que contienen gluten (trigo, centeno, cebada, avena)
allergen_rules.declaration_method: Bold in ingredient list AND 'Contiene:' statement after ingredient list.

weights_measures.net_weight_position: Principal display panel or information panel

language_requirements.minimum_font: Minimum 2mm character height for mandatory declarations

prohibited_claims: Advertising of products with ALTO EN seals to children under 14 via TV, internet, or public spaces
Sale or distribution of products with ALTO EN seals in schools
Free toys, prizes, or gifts with products carrying ALTO EN seals (directed at children)
special_requirements: Chile's ALTO EN octagonal seal system is legally mandatory since 2016 — the FIRST country globally to mandate this
Advertising restrictions for products with ALTO EN seals are strictly enforced by MINSAL and CNTV
School kiosks may not sell products with any ALTO EN seal
Marketing using cartoon characters or child-directed advertising restricted for products with seals
RS number from ISP mandatory on all packaged food labels
June 2019: Phase 3 of law implemented stricter threshold levels and expanded advertising restrictions
labeling_requirements.enforcement_notes: SEREMIS de Salud conduct regular market surveillance. Products with ALTO EN seals found in schools trigger significant fines. ISP can cancel RS for persistent non-compliance. Chile's Law 20.606 has been extensively studied globally as a model for public health food labeling.

mandatory_fields: Octágonos de advertencia (ALTO EN: mandatory since 2019/2021)
Nombre y domicilio del fabricante/importador peruano

nutrition_declaration.format: Per 100g/100mL. % VRN. Octagonal warning seals mandatory on FRONT of pack if: energy >300 kcal/100g (solid), sugars >10g/100g, saturated fat >4g/100g, sodium >400mg/100g. Peru thresholds are STRICTER than Chile.
nutrition_declaration.nrv_reference: Peru Valores de Referencia de Nutrientes per DS 038-2014-SA
nutrition_declaration.warning_seals: ALTO EN: AZÚCARES, SODIO, GRASAS SATURADAS, GRASAS TRANS — black octagonal seals mandatory with lower thresholds than Chile

allergen_rules.regulatory_basis: DS 007-98-SA — Reglamento de Vigilancia y Control Sanitario (Alérgenos)

language_requirements.note: Quechua and other indigenous language translations encouraged but not mandatory

prohibited_claims: Advertising products with ALTO EN seals to minors in media, schools, or public spaces
Disease cure/treatment claims without DIGEMID authorisation
Claims that minimize health impact of warning seals

claim_rules.organico: SENASA (Servicio Nacional de Sanidad Agraria) organic certification

special_requirements: Peru's Ley 30021 warning seals have STRICTER thresholds than Chile — more products will bear seals
Full enforcement including advertising restrictions since June 2021
RS number from DIGESA mandatory on all food product labels
Schools must not sell or promote products with ALTO EN seals
Restaurants with >10 locations must post caloric content on menus
labeling_requirements.enforcement_notes: DIGESA and DIGEMID conduct surveillance. Peru's octagonal seal enforcement has been stronger than many expected. INDECOPI enforces fair competition aspects. Significant fines for non-compliance.
